app.title: qPilot
app.summary: A person opens an instrument's raw amplification-curve file or a table of cycle values. They review proposals for what each sample and target is, accepting, editing or rejecting each one with a reason, and confirm the design. Group results stay hidden until this step is done. Next they check every well's curve and amplification call on a plate map and confirm the curves. The tool then runs every reasonable combination of analysis settings and shows how often each gene's call holds. Only the choices that could change a conclusion come up as cards, and the person decides each one with a reason. The result leaves as a report, tables, figures and a hash-chained record of every decision that anyone can re-run.

task.text: Turn raw qPCR curves into per-gene expression calls, and make a person decide, with a reason on record, each analysis choice that could change a conclusion.

data.text: Raw amplification curves from multi-well plates across many runs, a study design that assigns samples to groups and genes to roles, and the decisions people make about analysis choices
data.item: a well on a qPCR plate, with its amplification curve, its sample and its target gene

stage.text: analysing raw instrument curves into group comparisons, and deciding the analysis choices before reporting

mechanism.text: A section rail leads through the stages in order (design, curves, results, record), and each stage stays locked until the one before it is confirmed. Proposals arrive in a review inbox with accept or reject and a reason. A plate map is linked to a curve viewer for the wells. Results combine a robustness map of every gene, a matrix of which choices flip which calls, and decision cards that wait for the person. Exports and a verifiable record close the work.

field.text: relative quantification of gene expression by qPCR, with a robustness check across analysis choices, in molecular biology

workflow.name: settle the analysis choices that could change a conclusion, and record who decided

steps.here: Drop an RDML file, an instrument export set or a Cq table, optionally with a sample sheet and one sentence about the experiment, or open the demo study.

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: Rules or a model propose each sample's group and type and each gene's role, and the engine marks each proposal consistent or contradicted. The person accepts, edits or rejects each one with a reason, or sets the design on the plate, then confirms the stage.

With the plate map coloured by call, Cq or efficiency, the person clicks a well to see its amplification and melt curves. Where the Curve Judge disagrees with LinRegPCR, the call comes up as a proposal to keep or override, and the person confirms the curves.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Every combination of reference-gene set, group cut-off, empty-well rule and amplification rule is analysed. Each gene gets a fold change, a call and the share of analyses that give the same call, drawn on the robustness map and the flip matrix.
Decision Cards list only the choices that change at least one call, each option with the genes it flips. The person picks an option with a reason and then confirms all the analysis choices.

The Report section exports an Excel workbook, CSV tables, a figure per gene or a journal supplement. The Record section exports a checksummed, hash-chained zip of the input, the results and every decision.

distinctive: Results are blind: nothing that pairs a group with a number is shown until a person has confirmed both the design and the curves, and the server enforces this.
Every reasonable analysis is run, and only the choices that flip a conclusion are put to the person; the software settles only the choices that change nothing.
AI or rule proposals are checked by a deterministic engine, but only a person can accept them, and an AI agent's requests always wait for a person.
Every decision is written with its reason and who made it into a hash-chained record that can be verified and re-run byte for byte.
